title: Benefits Navigator knowledge-base entry
description: Contract for a versioned, source-linked program entry (BN-04/HACK-29). Every fact a user can see must trace to an official source with a retrieval date, and stale or withdrawn entries must never be cited silently: the consuming API surfaces the entry status alongside any fact it shows.

id.description: Snake_case identifier, unique across the knowledge base.

title.description: Human-readable program name. Carries the {{PILOT_PROGRAM}} placeholder until a pilot is chosen.

version.description: Monotonically increasing integer. Bump when any fact or source changes; citations surface the version they came from.

status.description: State rules. active: facts re-verified against the sources; citable with status and retrieval date shown. stale: sources may have changed since retrieval; must never be cited silently - any surfaced fact must display the stale status and the status_reason. withdrawn: retracted entirely (program ended, source disowned the facts, or a retraction was found); must never be cited as fact, only presented as withdrawn, and always with the status_reason.

status_reason.description: Why the entry is stale or withdrawn. Required for stale and withdrawn entries so a non-active citation can always say why.

superseded_by.description: Id of the entry that replaces this one. Set when a replacement exists.

iso_date.description: Calendar date the referenced content was retrieved or re-verified (ISO 8601, YYYY-MM-DD). Consumers surface this date with any fact they show.

https_url.description: Official source URL (government or program authority), https only. Placeholders like https://example.org/{{PILOT_PROGRAM}}/rules stand in until a pilot is chosen.

source_id.description: Id of one of this entry's sources (cross-checked in code; JSON Schema cannot express the reference).

supports.description: What this source supports in the entry.

due.description: ISO date when fixed; otherwise a statement the listed source supports.

signal_fact_group.description: Optional group (mission v2 M3): what this entry's official rules consider about a person, expressed over the generic question spec. Deterministic match scoring consumes these; each carries the program-side reason a card can show, backed by the group's source. Question ids must resolve in specs/question-spec (cross-checked in tests, not here).

question_id.description: Id of a question in the generic question spec this signal evaluates.

values.description: Option values the signal matches on. Omitted: any known, non-blank answer matches.

weight.description: How strongly this signal counts toward the entry's score. Default 1.

reason.description: Program-side claim shown on the match card when the signal matches, backed by the group's source.

cadence_fact_group.description: Optional group (BN-22 renewal tracker): how often the program renews coverage, machine-readable so the app can estimate a next renewal date from a date the person reports. Every estimate cites its schedule's source (the item's source_id when it has one, else this group's) and is labeled as an estimate, never as an official date. Item ids must be unique within the group, and an item's source_id must name one of the entry's sources (both cross-checked in code and tests; JSON Schema cannot express them).

id.description: Snake_case schedule id, unique within the group.

interval_months.description: Months between renewals under this schedule.

label.description: The schedule in plain language, as the schedule's source states it.

applies_to.description: Who the schedule's source says this schedule covers, in plain language.

ages.description: The ages the source says this schedule covers, inclusive (min must not exceed max; checked in code). Omitted: the source names no age range. The tracker asks one on-device question about it and leaves the schedule out of the estimates when the answer is outside the range.
